prompts.content:
STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)
Before writing a single word of narration or any image prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic and Source Material. Do not skip this. A shallow script produces a failed video.

Research silently and establish:

Verified core facts — what actually happened, who was involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, and popular myth.

The single strongest HOOK ANGLE — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for.

The core EMOTION of this episode (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.

Visual opportunities — which 3–5 moments are inherently cinematic and what each looks like (era, location, costume, light, scale).

Uncertainties — anything sources disagree on or you cannot verify. NEVER invent quotations, Sanskrit verses, dates, statistics, dialogue from scripture, or miracles presented as scientific proof. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly.

Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation.

🕉️ RAMAYANA — ADI KAVYA
MASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 8.0 HYBRID CINEMATIC (Scene 1 Video Hook)
Bible + Script Prompt + Hybrid Cinematic Production Prompt + Workflow Guide, in one document — Cinematic Video Hook Edition
This single file merges the original documents into one complete visual production system with a mandatory Scene 1 Video Hook to maximize viewer retention.

🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL (Narration + Visuals + Motion Graphics / Metadata)
This pipeline enforces a strict THREE-TAG SYSTEM:

1. Audio Narration Tag: Exactly one <script>...</script> block housing the clean TTS-ready narration in Section 2B. Spoken Devanagari Hindi only.

2. Sequential Visual Tags (Numbered Timeline):
- Scene 1 Hook: <video_prompt1>...</video_prompt1> — Mandatory 9:16 continuous cinematic video prompt (80–120 words) with camera movement to hook cold viewers immediately so they stay.
- Subsequent Story Stills: <image_prompt2>, <image_prompt3>, up to <image_prompt[N]> with real-time dynamic motion graphics.
- Thumbnail Tag: <image_prompt0> strictly reserved for the external promotional cover/thumbnail.
- Crucial Rule on <image_prompt0>: Index 0 is strictly reserved for the external promotional cover/thumbnail (16:9). It is never placed inside the video editing timeline.
- Story Stills: The actual narrative starts at <image_prompt1> and increments continuously through scene stills, the Follow Frame, and the End Card.

3. Real-Time Dynamic Motion Graphics Tags:
Sequential <motion_graphic1>, <motion_graphic2>, ... <motion_graphic[N]> (or <metadata[N]>) tags specifying real-time dynamic motion graphics.
The script AI decides in real time WHEN, WHERE, and WHICH TYPE of motion graphics is required based on the sacred story beats.
Crucial Rule: You are NOT limited to any template catalog or canned IDs! You can invent and specify ANY type of motion graphic that elevates the story (e.g. sacred_shloka_revelation, divine_astra_focus, celestial_timeline_dial, dharma_wisdom_punch, cosmic_metric_counter, sacred_vow_seal, etc.).

For each motion graphic, specify:
- #scene: The scene number where the graphic triggers
- Type: Any creative descriptive type chosen by the AI
- When: Exact contiguous cue phrase from the spoken narration that triggers the graphic
- Where: Screen placement (center, top, bottom, left, right, custom coordinates) respecting negative space
- Title: The primary headline or Sanskrit/Devanagari phrase
- Detail: Translation, spiritual meaning, or context
- Visual: Aesthetic styling and kinetic concept (e.g. 24k gold leaf calligraphy, luminous aura bloom, sacred vector linework, particle dissipation)

Example Format:
<motion_graphic1>
#scene 2
Type: sacred_vow_seal
When: [Exact contiguous spoken cue phrase from scene narration]
Where: top
Title: [Sacred Title / Mantra, e.g. उत्तिष्ठ राम]
Detail: [Spiritual context / meaning, e.g. तात जनक का संताप मिटाओ]
Visual: Sacred royal golden seal with radiant halo rays and glowing Devanagari lettering
</motion_graphic1>

All AI video, motion prompts, and animation directions are completely removed. Every visual asset is a detailed, static prompt.

📑 TABLE OF CONTENTS
WORKFLOW GUIDE — how to use this file

THE BIBLE — static reference (Character Bible, Location Bible, Visual Style, Religious Accuracy Law, Negative Prompt, Style Tags)

SCRIPT PROMPT — creative pass (run first)

PRODUCTION PROMPT — asset pass (run second)

PART 1 — 🕉️ WORKFLOW GUIDE
How to Use the Split System
THE THREE DOCUMENTS (Parts of this one file)
THE BIBLE — Static reference. Contains: Character Bible, Location Bible, Visual Style, Religious Accuracy Law, Universal Negative Prompt, Universal Style Tags.

THE SCRIPT PROMPT — Creative pass. Run FIRST. Output: locked Hindi script (Sections 1, 2, 2B) with Section 2B wrapped in <script>...</script>.

THE PRODUCTION PROMPT — HYBRID CINEMATIC ASSET PASS (SCENE 1 ALWAYS VIDEO). Run SECOND. Takes locked script + Bible → outputs a cinematic moving video prompt in <video_prompt1> for the opening hook, and static visual prompts in <image_prompt[n]> tags with real-time dynamic motion graphics in <metadata[n]> tags plus overlays and reflection prompts (Sections 3, 4, 5). Scene 1 is always a dynamic video to hook viewers immediately and maximize retention.

WORKFLOW PER VIDEO
STEP 1: PREPARE INPUTS
Provide:

Plaintext
Type: A (Story) or B (Fact)
Title: [Optional — if not provided, AI generates from content]
Content: [The story or fact content]
STEP 2: RUN SCRIPT PROMPT
Paste Script Prompt + your content input.

Section 1: Full script with scenes, timing, emotion beats, on-screen text

Section 2: ElevenLabs TTS script with timestamps

Section 2B: Paste-ready voiced script for ElevenLabs, wrapped in <script>...</script>

STEP 3: RUN PRODUCTION PROMPT
Paste Production Prompt + Locked Script (including <script> block) + Bible reference.

Section 3: Detailed static image prompts (<image_prompt0> for Thumbnail, <image_prompt1> to <image_prompt[N]> for scenes, Follow Frame, and End Card)

Section 4: Hindi text overlays for the editor

Section 5: Reflection Engine prompt for audience engagement

STEP 4: PRODUCE
Generate every visual in Leonardo.AI using Section 3 prompts (copy inside each <image_prompt[n]> block).

Record narration in ElevenLabs using the Section 2B script (copy inside <script> block).

Assemble in editor: narration + static images + Section 4 overlays.

Post with the reflection question from Section 5.

PART 2 — 🕉️ THE BIBLE (Static Reference)
👥 CHARACTER BIBLE — NEVER CHANGE THESE DESCRIPTIONS
Copy relevant character details into EVERY image prompt.

🔵 RAMA
Age: 25–30 years old

Skin: Deep blue-dark complexion ("shyama varna") — non-negotiable, never fair

Face: Strong jaw, high forehead, calm and powerful eyes, slightly arched eyebrows

Body: Tall, broad shoulders, long arms reaching knees ("ajanubahu")

Hair: Long black hair tied in an ascetic knot (jata) or warrior bun

Palace attire: Yellow/gold silk dhoti, ornate crown (mukut), gold jewelry, bow Sharanga

Forest/Exile attire: Ochre/saffron bark-cloth dhoti, matted hair, no crown, bow and quiver

Expression: Dignified, compassionate, serene, divine majesty — never angry or anxious

🌟 SITA
Age: 20–25 years old

Skin: Golden-fair radiant complexion ("suvarna varna")

Face: Large expressive eyes, gentle grace, oval face, long black hair

Palace attire: Rich red and gold silk saree, elaborate traditional jewelry

Forest attire: Simple ochre or cream cotton saree, minimal wooden/seed jewelry, braided hair

Lanka captivity attire: Worn pale saree, unadorned, solemn dignity, sorrowful yet resilient eyes

Expression: Graceful, resolute, devoted — never weak or helpless

🏹 LAKSHMANA
Age: 22–27 years old

Skin: Fair wheatish complexion

Face: Sharp warrior features, intense alert eyes, strong jaw

Body: Highly athletic, muscular build

Attire: Similar to Rama's palette in green/ochre, carrying formidable longbow and quiver

Expression: Fiercely vigilant, protective, intense loyalty

🐒 HANUMAN
Form: Powerful Vanara warrior, golden-orange fur, upright muscular physique, tail arched gracefully

Attire: Simple sacred loincloth (kaupin), sacred thread (janeu), mace (gada)

Expression: Deep devotional surrender, awe-inspiring strength, humble eyes

Scale: Explicitly specify normal human scale OR mountain-sized colossal form (vishwaroopa)

👑 RAVANA
Age: 40–50 years old appearance — imposing sovereign

Skin: Dark bronze with fiery crimson undertone

Face: Ten heads (in wide establishing shots) OR dominant majestic central head (in close-ups)

Attire: Black and blood-red royal silk, heavy gold armor, jeweled crowns, multiple armed weapons

Expression: Regal arrogance, unyielding pride, formidable authority — never cartoonish

🗺️ LOCATION BIBLE
Ayodhya Palace: Treta Yuga Vedic stone architecture, colossal carved pillars, oil lamps, marigold drapes, sacred havan smoke, warm amber-gold light.

Dandaka / Panchavati Forest: Dense primordial Indian jungle, towering sal/banyan trees, hanging roots, morning mist, sacred thatched ashram hut with a quiet dhuni fire.

Chitrakuta: Peaceful sacred hills, clear streams, gentle deer, untouched natural serenity.

Lanka: Imposing black stone and gold architecture atop jagged sea-cliffs, towering spires, dramatic stormy or twilight skies.

Ashoka Vatika: Melancholic royal garden, weeping ashoka trees with scarlet blooms, oppressive luxury framing captivity.

Kishkindha: Massive granite caves, carved mountain redoubts, waterfalls, primitive grandeur.

Ram Setu / Ocean Shore: Craggy shoreline, endless churning ocean, massive floating sandstone boulders inscribed with holy names, vast Vanara host.

⚠️ RELIGIOUS ACCURACY LAW
Rama must always have blue-dark skin.

Treta Yuga setting only: absolute zero modern elements, modern clothing, or foreign architecture.

Sacred Vedic attributes (tilak, janeu, agni, mudras) must be visually accurate.

🖼️ UNIVERSAL NEGATIVE PROMPT
Plaintext
cartoon, anime, 3d render, illustration, modern clothing, modern architecture, western facial features, plastic skin, wrong skin color for Rama (must be blue-dark, never fair), light-skinned Rama, disrespectful depiction, blurry, watermark, text in image, extra limbs, deformed hands, distorted anatomy
🖼️ UNIVERSAL STYLE TAGS
Plaintext
ultra realistic, cinematic photography, Treta Yuga ancient India, devotional epic atmosphere, volumetric lighting, photorealistic textures, 8K resolution, emotionally powerful composition, sacred grandeur
[ANCIENT DHARMA EDITORIAL RULES]
Apply these writing rules to Ancient Dharma episodes. For an explicitly unrelated topic, follow that topic's own tradition and audience instead of adding Hindu devotional language. These rules update the research, narration and closing instructions below; preserve every existing output section, extraction tag, asset number, media mode, character bible and narration-to-scene mapping. Perform the editorial work silently; do not add a new output section.

RESEARCH BEFORE COMMITTING TO A HOOK: Identify the actual source/version, what it supports, what belongs to a regional retelling, and what is interpretation. Establish one central dilemma, the strongest supported detail, the decisive choice and the real outcome. Treat any preselected retention hook as provisional: revise its wording and promise when the research does not support it. Never invent dialogue, motives, quotations, miracles as scientific proof, or scriptural attribution to make a hook work. Keep source notes in the existing production notes, with a brief natural attribution in speech where necessary.

OPEN INSIDE THE STORY: Compare three distinct, truthful openings internally: an action, a contradiction, and a consequential choice. Choose the clearest one, rather than always opening with a long 'why' question. Name the person or sacred object and make the situation understandable without the title. Match the first visible image/action to the first spoken words; no introductory temple montage or scenery before the predicament. The next sentence must advance that same event or give a useful clue, not restart with biography or a history lecture.

FORWARD MOMENTUM: Write simple, natural spoken Devanagari Hindi with devotional dignity. Every sentence must add necessary context, an action, discovery, obstacle, decision or consequence. Connect beats through cause and effect. Give intermediate answers; do not save every useful detail for the ending. Remove repeated praise, repeated explanations, abstract moral lectures, excessive adjectives and empty suspense. Preserve emotional breaths; never rush speech or add filler to satisfy a duration. Build emotion from supported events, not invented private thoughts.

SHORTS: Tell one complete dilemma and resolution, not an entire biography. Establish the concrete situation in the first short sentence and give a clue or consequence in the next one or two. Use a genuine discovery or consequential choice near the midpoint when the story needs it; do not force a twist or repeated question. Resolve the opening promise with the decisive action, reason and outcome, then move directly to the closing invitation.

ONE VARIED ENGAGEMENT CLOSE: After the complete story payoff, include ONE compact Hindi closing invitation asking viewers to like the video, subscribe to Ancient Dharma, and leave ONE specific comment. Allow approximately 5–8 seconds within the selected Shorts runtime; reserve this speech time before drafting the story. Do not try to squeeze all three requests into a three-second blessing. Keep it warm and direct, without interrupting the story or adding separate spoken like, subscribe, blessing and end-card sequences.

VARY THE COMMENT REQUEST: Choose either a short devotional response appropriate to the episode or one easy, concrete question about its central choice. Vary the response AND the sentence structure across topics; examples are alternatives, not a fixed closing to copy into every video. Ram-focused episodes may invite 'जय श्री राम' or 'सीताराम'; Hanuman-focused episodes may invite 'जय बजरंगबली' or 'जय हनुमान'; Shiva-focused episodes may invite 'हर हर महादेव' or 'ॐ नमः शिवाय'; Krishna-focused episodes may invite 'राधे कृष्ण' or 'जय श्री कृष्ण'. Never force a Ram greeting into an unrelated tradition. For a dilemma, ask a brief question such as 'भरत के किस निर्णय ने आपको सबसे अधिक छुआ?' instead of a generic 'आपकी क्या राय है?'. Invite one response, not a list of questions.

Possible closing patterns, adapted to the episode rather than repeated verbatim: 'कमेंट में जय श्री राम लिखिए। कथा अच्छी लगी तो लाइक करें और Ancient Dharma को सब्सक्राइब करें।' / 'हनुमान जी की भक्ति को नमन—कमेंट में जय बजरंगबली! ऐसी कथाओं के लिए लाइक करें और चैनल सब्सक्राइब करें।' / 'भरत के किस निर्णय ने आपका मन छुआ? कमेंट में बताइए, वीडियो लाइक करें और चैनल से जुड़ने के लिए सब्सक्राइब करें।' Use natural Hindi pronunciation of the channel name in speech if needed. Make the invitation compelling through relevance, never guilt, threats, guaranteed blessings, promised miracles, or claims that a 'true devotee' must engage. Do not demand repeated comments, personal information, or a subscription in exchange for the answer.

SYNC AND SILENT CHECK: Put the closing words exactly once in the clean voice script and their matching final CTA narration segment(s), using the existing tags and timeline format. Reuse existing follow/end-card slots where present; they form one close, not additional speeches or silent padding. Overlays must match the selected comment request and must not add conflicting engagement demands. Check that the opening is specific, the next sentence advances it, the source supports the claim, the middle develops, the payoff is complete before the CTA, and the close includes like + subscribe + one episode-relevant comment invitation. Do not output these checks or predict retention scores.
[/ANCIENT DHARMA EDITORIAL RULES]

PART 3 — 🕉️ SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass — Run FIRST)
Take raw content and output a locked Hindi script. Never generate images or visual prompts in this pass.

Content Setup & Rules
Hook Rule: The first 3–6 spoken words must begin a concrete, source-supported action, dilemma or contrast with immediate emotional stakes. Complete a clear opening thought within the first 1–3 seconds; name the relevant person or sacred object instead of a vague "this" or "he". Let the unanswered question arise from why the action matters, not from hiding who is involved. No channel greetings, series titles, background lecture or invented sacred dialogue. Keep the central question clear while giving an early concrete answer, clue or consequence in the next one or two sentences. Every following sentence must change what the viewer knows, what the protagonist can do, or what the choice will cost. Connect beats through cause and effect; cut repeated setup, biography before the predicament, redundant adjectives and generic suspense. Aim for a meaningful development about every 5–8 seconds where the story supports it, inside the existing scene structure; this is a writing guide, not a cut, scene-count or speech-speed requirement. Use short, natural spoken sentences, clear subjects and concrete verbs. Never hide basic context just to manufacture curiosity. Silently compare three different opening lines and use the clearest, most specific one that the story actually pays off; output only the chosen line in the existing format. Read the opening without the title: the viewer must understand the situation and have a specific reason to hear the next sentence. Remove any line that adds neither necessary context nor a new development. These are editorial choices, not guaranteed audience metrics.

Midpoint Re-Hook: At 50–60% mark, use a concise source-supported discovery, decision or consequence that changes the meaning of an earlier detail or raises the cost of the next action. Follow the 5–8 word turn with its concrete explanation; do not merely announce that a twist is coming. Preserve devotional dignity and source fidelity. A smaller resolved question should lead naturally into the remaining central question.

Language: Simple, poignant, spoken Devanagari Hindi with temple-katha resonance.

Ending: Complete the story and its promised payoff first. Then give ONE varied Hindi closing invitation to like, subscribe and leave one episode-relevant comment, following the editorial rules above. Reserve approximately 5–8 seconds within the selected runtime. Use the existing follow/end-card slots as one close; no separate repeated blessing, recap or extra engagement requests. Finish the story on its concrete consequence before the invitation.



SECTION 1 — SCRIPT BREAKDOWN (Production Planning)
Provide scene-by-scene script blocks:

Duration: [X seconds]
Emotion: [Devotion / Awe / Grief / Resolve]

Tone: [Devotional / Tense / Whispered / Majestic]

SECTION 2 — ELEVENLABS TIMESTAMPS
Narration with timing blocks (every 6–10 seconds) for editorial sync.

SECTION 2B — ELEVENLABS COMPLETE VOICED SCRIPT (PASTE-READY)
The complete narration must be enclosed in exactly one <script>...</script> tag. No markdown, no timestamps, no speaker tags inside.

Plaintext

(break)

</script>
PART 4 — 🕉️ PRODUCTION PROMPT (Static Asset Pass — Run SECOND)
Your ONLY job is to take the LOCKED script and generate all STATIC visual assets, motion graphics metadata, and engagement text.

Rules:
Scene 1 MUST ALWAYS be a video (<video_prompt1>) with dynamic camera movement to hook cold viewers immediately.

Every prompt is a high-detail static shot description (70–140 words).

Thumbnail is wrapped in <image_prompt0>.

Scene images are wrapped in auto-incrementing tags: <image_prompt1>, <image_prompt2>, ... <image_prompt[N]>.

High-retention motion graphics are wrapped in auto-incrementing tags: <metadata1>, <metadata2>, ... <metadata[N]> (scripture scrolls, era timelines, sacred maps, relic reticles, canto titles).

SECTION 3 — LEONARDO.AI STATIC IMAGE PROMPTS
Follow the numbering strictly:

<image_prompt0>: 16:9 Thumbnail

<image_prompt1> to <image_prompt[N]>: Scene Stills, Follow Frame, End Card

Prompt Tag Structure:

SECTION 4 — HINDI TEXT OVERLAYS (VIDEO EDITOR REFERENCE)
Provide clean, on-screen text overlays matching each visual scene:

Thumbnail Text: 3–5 high-impact Devanagari words.

Opening Frame Text: 2–4 words carrying the core emotion.

Scene Lower-Thirds: Optional concise chapter labels.

Follow Frame Text: One concise CTA overlay matching this episode’s selected comment invitation plus like/subscribe; vary the devotional phrase or story question. Do not always use the same slogan.

End Card Text: A short episode-appropriate closing phrase within the same CTA, without an additional speech or extended silent hold.

SECTION 5 — THE REFLECTION ENGINE
Provide one sacred, heartfelt question based on the episode's core emotion to pin in the YouTube comments:

Focuses on human feelings (sacrifice, duty, loss, devotion) rather than controversial moral debate.

Phrased in gentle, respectful Hindi.

✅ PRODUCTION COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST
[ ] Exactly THREE tag types are used: <script> for narration, <image_prompt[n]> for visuals, and <metadata[n]> for motion graphics.

[ ] Section 2B has exactly one <script>...</script> tag containing only Devanagari text.

[ ] Thumbnail is enclosed in <image_prompt0>...</image_prompt0> and omitted from the timeline.

[ ] Scene images increment without gaps: <image_prompt1>, <image_prompt2>, etc.

[ ] Motion graphics metadata tags are provided (<metadata1>, <metadata2>, etc.) for key story beats.

[ ] Scene 1 has a dedicated cinematic <video_prompt1> continuous shot prompt.

[ ] Full Character Bible descriptions are repeated verbatim inside every relevant prompt.

graphics.style: Let AI choose only moments where a graphic materially explains the narration. Metadata is a suggestion, never a command to decorate every scene. Leave ordinary footage clean, keep breathing room between beats, and allow zero graphics. No cards, panels, boxed labels, enclosing frames, blur backings or photo badges. Use free-floating type, fine lines and purposeful diagrams in open space around subjects. Never invent facts, coordinates, source labels or telemetry. Preview the actual result before export.

generatedAudio.narrationText:
[कुंती]: कर्ण, युद्ध रोकने से पहले तुम्हें जानना होगा कि तुम सूतपुत्र नहीं, मेरे सबसे बड़े ज्येष्ठ पुत्र हो!

[कर्ण]: ज्येष्ठ पुत्र? देवी कुंती, यह आप क्या कह रही हैं? मैं तो सूत अधिरथ और माता राधा का पुत्र हूँ!

[कुंती]: नहीं पुत्र! तुम सूर्यदेव के मंत्र-वरदान से जन्मे मेरे प्रथम कौन्तेय हो! लोक-लज्जा के भय में मैंने तुम्हें गंगा में बहा दिया था!

[कर्ण]: माता... जब सारा संसार मुझे सूतपुत्र कहकर अपमानित कर रहा था, तब आपकी ममता कहाँ सोई थी?

[कुंती]: वह मेरी जीवन की सबसे बड़ी भूल थी, कर्ण! आज मुझे क्षमा कर दो और अपने भाइयों के पास लौट आओ!

[कर्ण]: आज जब युद्ध सामने खड़ा है, तब आप मुझे मेरा राजकुल और अधिकार याद दिलाने आई हैं?

[कुंती]: हस्तिनापुर का मुकुट तुम्हारा है पुत्र! युधिष्ठिर और अर्जुन तुम्हारे चरण धोकर तुम्हें सम्राट बनाएंगे!

[कर्ण]: जिस दुर्योधन ने मुझे सम्मान, मित्रता और अंगदेश का राज्य दिया, क्या इस अंतिम घड़ी में मैं उसे धोखा दे दूँ?

[कुंती]: तो क्या तुम अपने ही सगे पांडव भाइयों का रक्त बहाओगे? क्या तुम अपनी माता की गोद सूनी करोगे?

[कर्ण]: मित्रद्रोह महापाप है माता! मैं दुर्योधन का पक्ष छोड़कर अधर्म और कायरता का कलंक नहीं ले सकता!

[कुंती]: तो क्या मेरा ज्येष्ठ पुत्र मेरे ही कुल का विनाश देखेगा? कर्ण, मुझे खाली हाथ मत लौटाओ!

[कर्ण]: कर्ण के द्वार से उसकी माता कभी खाली हाथ नहीं जाएगी! मैं आपको अपना पवित्र वचन देता हूँ!

[कुंती]: कैसा वचन, कर्ण? कहो पुत्र, तुम क्या प्रतिज्ञा करते हो?

[कर्ण]: मैं युधिष्ठिर, भीम, नकुल और सहदेव पर बाण नहीं चलाऊँगा! वे रणभूमि में मेरे सामने आएंगे, तब भी मैं उन्हें अभयदान दूँगा!

[कुंती]: और अर्जुन? क्या तुम अर्जुन को छोड़ोगे?

[कर्ण]: युद्ध केवल मेरे और अर्जुन के बीच होगा! या तो कर्ण रहेगा या अर्जुन... आपके पाँच पुत्र सदा जीवित रहेंगे! इस अमर वचन के लिए वीडियो लाइक करें, Ancient Dharma को सब्सक्राइब करें और 'जय श्री कृष्ण' लिखें!

researchData:
# RESEARCH DOSSIER: KARNA AND KUNTI ON THE BANKS OF THE GANGA (THE SECRET TRUTH & THE OATH OF FIVE SONS)

---

## 1. VERIFIED FACTS, BACKGROUND & KEY DATA

### Scriptural Origin & Context
* **Primary Source:** Vyasa Mahabharata, *Udyoga Parva* (specifically the *Kunti-Karna Samvada* section, preceding the Kurukshetra War).
* **Setting:** The sacred banks of the River Ganga at Hastinapur (or near the bathing ghats/sandbanks where Karna performs his afternoon solar worship / *Sandhyavandanam*).
* **Core Historical/Epic Context:** As war becomes inevitable after Krishna's failed peace mission, Queen Kunti decides to approach Karna to reveal his divine birth, hoping to bring him to the Pandava side, prevent brotherly bloodshed, and save both Karna and her other sons.

### Key Characters & Emotional Matrix
1. **Karna (Angaraja / Radheya / Kaunteya):**
   * *Status:* King of Anga, loyal general and soulmate friend of Duryodhana. Known as *Suta-putra* (charioteer's son) by society.
   * *Inner Conflict:* Deep-seated trauma from societal rejection vs. absolute gratitude and unshakeable loyalty to Duryodhana, who gave him dignity, kingdom, and honor when the world cast him out.
   * *Dharmic Stance:* Cannot abandon Duryodhana at the hour of war, even upon learning he is the eldest Pandava and heir to the throne of Indraprastha/Hastinapur.
2. **Kunti (Pritha):**
   * *Status:* Dowager Queen of the Pandavas, mother of Yudhisthira, Bhima, and Arjuna (and stepmother to Nakula and Sahadeva).
   * *Inner Conflict:* Motherly guilt for abandoning her divine newborn infant (conceived via Surya Deva's mantra boon) in a floating basket on the Ganga out of fear of social stigma.
   * *Dharmic Stance:* Desperate mother attempting to avert the annihilation of her lineage by uniting her eldest son (Karna) with his younger brothers.

### Sacred Dialogue & Critical Narrative Turning Points
* **The Revelation:** Kunti approaches Karna as he stands in prayer facing the rising/midday sun. She reveals that he is not the son of Adhiratha and Radha, but her firstborn, fathered by the Sun God (*Surya Deva*), making him the rightful eldest Pandava (*Kaunteya*).
* **The Offer:** Kunti offers him the throne, the empire, and the love and submission of his five younger brothers (Yudhisthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva).
* **The Emotional Clash & Rejection:** Karna respectfully acknowledges his mother, but calls out her abandonment. He explains that switching sides now on the eve of war would be cowardice and betrayal (*Mitra-droha*) to Duryodhana, who stood by him when Kunti abandoned him.
* **The Tragic Compromise / The Oath of Five Sons (*Pancha-Pandava Vachan*):** To ensure his mother does not return empty-handed, Karna grants her a solemn, fatal vow:
  * He will not kill Yudhisthira, Bhima, Nakula, or Sahadeva on the battlefield, despite having the power to do so.
  * He will fight only Arjuna to the death.
  * *Resulting Oath:* "Whether I die or Arjuna dies, Kunti will always remain the mother of five sons."

---

## 2. CHRONOLOGICAL STORY ARC & SCENE BEATS (~90 SECONDS)

### Dramatic Multi-Character Progression (100% Conversational Drama - No Narrator)

* **Scene 1: The Dramatic Revelation at the River Bank (~0–20s)**
  * *Visual:* Misty Ganga ghat at sunset/sunrise. Karna in magnificent golden armor (*Kavacha*) holding his bow, turning toward Kunti who approaches in royal grief with outstretched hands.
  * *Dialogue Opening:* 
    * **कुंती:** कर्ण! युद्ध रोकने से पहले तुम्हें जानना होगा कि तुम सूतपुत्र नहीं, मेरे सबसे बड़े ज्येष्ठ पुत्र हो!
    * **कर्ण:** ज्येष्ठ पुत्र? देवी कुंती, यह आप क्या कह रही हैं? मैं अधिरथ और राधा का पुत्र हूँ!
    * **कुंती:** नहीं पुत्र! तुम सूर्यदेव के वरदान से उत्पन्न मेरे प्रथम कौन्तेय हो! मेरे भय ने तुम्हें गंगा में बहा दिया था... मुझे क्षमा कर दो पुत्र!

* **Scene 2: The Core Emotional Conflict & Moral Choice (~20–45s)**
  * *Visual:* Close-up dramatic tracking. Karna’s eyes reflect intense heartbreak, betrayal, and unyielding nobility; Kunti weeping, placing her hand on his armored arm.
  * *Dialogue:*
    * **कर्ण:** माता... जब समाज मुझे सूतपुत्र कहकर नीचा दिखा रहा था, तब आपने अपना पुत्र क्यों नहीं कहा?
    * **कुंती:** मेरी भूल थी कर्ण! अब पांडव तुम्हारे चरण छुएंगे, हस्तिनापुर का सिंहासन तुम्हारा होगा! चलो मेरे साथ!
    * **कर्ण:** नहीं माता! जिस दुर्योधन ने मुझे सम्मान और अंगदेश का मुकुट दिया, युद्ध के इस मुहाने पर मैं उसे धोखा नहीं दे सकता!

* **Scene 3: The Fatal Bargain & The Oath of Five Sons (~45–75s)**
  * *Visual:* Karna folding his hands with majestic dignity, gesturing toward the sacred waters of the Ganga, swearing a holy oath while Kunti trembles in tearful resignation.
  * *Dialogue:*
    * **कुंती:** तो क्या तुम अपने ही भाइयों का वध करोगे, कर्ण?
    * **कर्ण:** नहीं माता, कर्ण की शरण में आई माँ खाली हाथ नहीं जाएगी! मैं प्रतिज्ञा करता हूँ—युधिष्ठिर, भीम, नकुल और सहदेव पर मैं बाण नहीं चलाऊँगा!
    * **कुंती:** और अर्जुन?
    * **कर्ण:** युद्ध केवल मेरे और अर्जुन के बीच होगा! या तो अर्जुन रहेगा या कर्ण... आपके पाँच पुत्र सदा जीवित रहेंगे!

* **Scene 4: Spiritual Realization & Resolving Payoff (~75–90s)**
  * *Visual:* Sunset light glistening on the Ganga river waters; Kunti touching Karna's head in reluctant blessing as he stands stoic, ready for his ultimate tragic destiny.
  * *Dialogue & CTA Integration:*
    * **कुंती:** धन्य हो तुम्हारी दानवीरता और धर्म, कर्ण! इतिहास तुम्हें जेष्ठ पांडव और सबसे बड़ा मित्र मानकर नमन करेगा!
    * **कर्ण:** प्रणाम माता! (Addressing Audience) कर्ण और कुंती के इस त्याग की अमर गाथा के लिए वीडियो को लाइक करें, Ancient Dharma को सब्सक्राइब करें और कमेंट में 'जय श्री कृष्ण' लिखें!

---

## 3. VISUAL & WORLD-BUILDING CANON

### Setting & Era
* **Location:** Banks of the sacred River Ganga near Hastinapur.
* **Atmosphere/Lighting:** Atmospheric ancient sunrise/sunset with golden sunbeams breaking through misty river vapor. Dramatic contrast between warm solar light (reflecting Karna’s divine lineage) and cool misty shadows.
* **Architecture:** Ancient stone river steps (*Ghats*), Vedic stone pillars, floating lotus petals, and distant Vedic forest foliage along the riverbank.

### Character Design & Costume Consistency
* **Karna:**
  * Tall, exceptionally athletic, regal Kshatriya warrior with radiant divine aura.
  * *Attire:* Imperial golden armor (*Kavacha*), glowing golden earrings (*Kundala*), silk lower garments in royal crimson and gold, high leather armguards.
  * *Props:* Golden composite longbow (*Vijaya* bow style), quiver of arrows, royal armlets.
* **Kunti:**
  * Elderly royal Queen Mother, dignified yet deeply sorrowful.
  * *Attire:* Draped white and pale gold royal Vedic saree/uttariya, minimal antique silver/gold widow/queen jewelry, pale exhausted complexion with tear-stained cheeks.

### Visual Style Rules (Hybrid Generation Ready)
* **Image Stills:** Deep emotional close-ups capturing psychological tension, tears, and heavy moral weight.
* **Video Sequences:** Kinetic motion—flowing Ganga waters, mist moving across stone steps, Karna’s royal cape fluttering in the river breeze, folding hands in prayer.

---

## 4. SCRIPTWRITER DIRECTIVES

1. **STRICT ZERO NARRATOR MANDATE (`[सूत्रधार]` IS BANNED):**
   * Do NOT include any narrator lines or voiceover commentary outside the characters.
   * Every single detail (the revelation of divine birth, the tragedy of abandonment, the loyalty to Duryodhana, and the Pancha-Pandava oath) MUST be delivered through dialogue between `[कुंती]` and `[कर्ण]`.

2. **CHARACTER DIALOGUE RULES:**
   * Use exact tags: `[कुंती]:` and `[कर्ण]:`.
   * Written entirely in pure, speakable Devanagari Hindi.
   * Dignified Vedic/Epic tone (*Dharmic Hindi*), yet natural, fluid, and dramatic. No English or modern slang.

3. **EXACT OPENING LINE REQUIREMENT:**
   * Scene 1 MUST begin immediately with Kunti’s high-stakes confrontation line:
     `कुंती: कर्ण, युद्ध रोकने से पहले तुम्हें जानना होगा कि तुम सूतपुत्र नहीं, मेरे सबसे बड़े ज्येष्ठ पुत्र हो!`

4. **100% FULL VIDEO SCENES:**
   * Every scene beat in the script generation must utilize procedural video prompts (`<video_prompt[N]>`) with high visual motion (flowing river, moving mist, dynamic cinematic tracking).

5. **COMPACT SINGLE CLOSING CTA:**
   * In the final scene, weave the channel engagement naturally into the characters' spoken conclusion:
     * Like + Subscribe + Comment request (`'जय श्री कृष्ण'` or specific question on Karna's choice).

prompts.name: Ramayana & Sacred Epics — Pure Multi-Character Dialogue Master Prompt (100% Video, Zero Narrator)
prompts.content:
STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (MANDATORY)
Before writing a single word of narration or dialogue, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic and Source Material (Valmiki Ramayana, Vyasa Mahabharata, or sacred Puranas).
Establish:
1. The central characters in this episode:
   - For Ramayana: Shri Ram & Lakshman, Sita & Ravana, Ram & Hanuman, Lakshman & Meghnad, Ram & Bharat, Sugriva & Vali, Kevat & Ram, Jatayu & Ravana, Angad & Ravana, Ram & Samudra Dev.
   - For Mahabharata / Puranas: Krishna & Arjuna, Karna & Krishna, Draupadi & Krishna, Bhishma & Duryodhana, Shiva & Parvati.
2. The core moral dilemma, intense confrontation, or decisive turning point.
3. The decisive truth, action, pledge, or divine realization that resolves the tension.

🎭 PURE MULTI-CHARACTER CONVERSATIONAL DRAMA (100% FULL VIDEO ONLY — ZERO NARRATOR MANDATE)
In this format, there is STRICTLY NO NARRATOR ([सूत्रधार]). The entire video is pure character dialogue between the key figures.

🚨 MANDATORY RULE #1 — ZERO NARRATOR MANDATE (NO [सूत्रधार] / NO NARRATOR):
- NEVER write [सूत्रधार] or [Narrator]!
- Every single line in <script> must be spoken directly by one of the characters ([लक्ष्मण], [राम], [सीता], [हनुमान], [रावण], [समुद्र], [केवट], [विभीषण], [कृष्ण], [अर्जुन], etc.).
- Characters speak directly to each other from second zero through the final closing sacred line.

🙏 SACRED CHARACTER DICTION & DIGNIFIED SCRIPTURAL HINDI:
- When ancient gods, avataras, and epic figures speak (Devi Sita, Sri Rama, Lakshmana, Ravana, Hanuman, Krishna), they must speak with supreme scriptural dignity, noble vocabulary, and sacred gravitas true to the Valmiki Ramayana and Ramcharitmanas.
- STRICTLY FORBIDDEN STREET SLANG & RUDE PRONOUNS: Never use 'तू', 'तेरा', 'तुझे', 'तूने', 'काय रे', 'अरे', or modern street insults!
- Even when confronting evil or expressing righteous fury:
  * Mata Sita addresses Ravana as 'दशानन', 'रे निशाचर', 'लंकेश्वर', 'अधर्मी', using dignified pronouns: 'तुम्हारा', 'तुम्हें'.
  * Ravana speaks with royal ego and sovereign pride ('सीता! त्रिलोक विजेता लंकापति...'), never cheap street slang.

⏱️ FLOW CLIP DURATION LIMIT (NEVER CUT OFF AUDIO):
- Every Google Flow (Veo 3.1) scene video clip is strictly ~8 seconds long.
- Spoken dialogue in each scene MUST be concise: strictly 10 to 16 Hindi words (~3.5 to 4.5 seconds of spoken speech).
- This leaves at least 3 seconds of calm ambient room before the scene ends.
- The concluding scene (Scene 10) must NEVER be an overloaded paragraph; it must be a concise, powerful sacred conclusion (10–12 words, e.g. '[सीता]: सत्य और धर्म की सदा विजय होती है! अधर्म का नाश निश्चित है। जय श्री राम!') so speech finishes cleanly without being abruptly cut off.

🎬 100% FULL VIDEO ONLY PROTOCOL (GOOGLE FLOW NATIVE AUDIOVISUAL GENERATION):
- EVERY scene in the episode MUST be a full video shot (<video_prompt[N]>), never a still image.
- Google Flow (Veo 3.1) co-generates the character video and spoken Hindi voice in a single pass with natural lip-sync matching the dialogue in quotes.
- In each <video_prompt[N]>, provide:
  1. Camera motion & framing (medium close-up, dynamic camera move, epic volumetric lighting).
  2. Character physical consistency.
  3. Google Flow Speech Command:
     "The character speaks clearly in an authentic Hindi voice with natural lip-sync, delivering the spoken Hindi dialogue: \"[Character]: [exact spoken Hindi line]\". Natural mouth and jaw movements in sync with the spoken Hindi words, clean vocal dialogue audio, ambient tone, no background music."

🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL:

1. Audio Narration Tag: Exactly ONE <script>...</script> block.
- Spoken Devanagari Hindi only.
- 100% character dialogue with zero [सूत्रधार].
- Alternating dialogue between characters.

2. Sequential Visual Tags (Numbered Timeline):
- Scene 1 Hook: ALWAYS <video_prompt1>...</video_prompt1> showing the opening character speaking their challenge.
- All subsequent scenes: <video_prompt2> to <video_prompt[N]> each showing the speaking character with explicit Google Flow lip/jaw articulation directions.
- Thumbnail: <image_prompt0> strictly reserved for the external 16:9 promotional cover.

howItWorks: AI dynamically writes character spoken dialogue and narrator action beats. Scene 1 always starts with a character hook line. Google Flow animates speaking character lips when talking, and silent cinematic reaction shots when narrator speaks. Audio uses native SSML breath pauses and 0.75x–1.25x dynamic lip articulation retiming.

STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)Before writing a single word of narration or any image/video prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic and Source Material. Do not skip this. A shallow script produces a failed video.Research silently and establish:Verified core facts — what actually happened, who was involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, and popular myth.The single strongest HOOK ANGLE — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for.The core EMOTION of this episode (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.Visual opportunities — which moments require static, frozen emotional weight and which demand continuous, cinematic motion (era, location, costume, light, scale, kinetic action).Uncertainties — anything sources disagree on or you cannot verify. NEVER invent quotations, Sanskrit verses, dates, statistics, dialogue from scripture, or miracles presented as scientific proof. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly.Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation.🕉️ RAMAYANA — ADI KAVYAMASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 8.0 HYBRID MIXED MEDIABible + Script Prompt + Mixed Production Prompt (Images & Videos) + Workflow GuideThis document establishes the HYBRID MIXED-SCRIPT PIPELINE. It combines static visual stills and cinematic generative AI video clips into a single chronological timeline.🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOLThe pipeline uses three and only three functional tag families:Narration Tag: <script>...</script> — Houses the complete, raw, TTS-ready Devanagari Hindi audio narration in Section 2B.Auto-Incrementing Visual Tags: Sequential visual prompts matching the exact timeline order across both static and moving formats:<image_prompt[N]>...</image_prompt[N]> for static frames (Midjourney, Flux, Leonardo.AI).<video_prompt[N]>...</video_prompt[N]> for motion shots (Runway Gen-3, Luma Dream Machine, Sora, Kling).Crucial Rule: The first scene (Scene 1) MUST ALWAYS be a video (<video_prompt1>) to hook the user immediately. The index counter [N] increments chronologically across the entire video regardless of asset type: e.g., <video_prompt1>, <image_prompt2>, <video_prompt3>, <image_prompt4>.Thumbnail Tag: Always locked to <image_prompt0>...</image_prompt0>.📑 TABLE OF CONTENTSWORKFLOW GUIDE — Mixed script rules and asset selectionTHE BIBLE — Static reference (Character Bible, Location Bible, Visual Style, Religious Accuracy Law, Negative Prompts)SCRIPT PROMPT — Creative pass (run first)PRODUCTION PROMPT — Mixed asset generation pass (run second)PART 1 — 🕉️ WORKFLOW GUIDEHow to Manage the Mixed Media PipelineDECISION MATRIX: IMAGE VS. VIDEONot every scene should be video. Overusing video creates visual fatigue, morphing artifacts, and pacing breaks. Distribute assets deliberately:Asset TypeBest Used ForProduction Standard<image_prompt[N]>Emotional portraits, theological/sacred moments, heavy-detail environments, dialogue pauses, moments requiring zero anatomical distortion.70–140 words, hyper-detailed composition, frozen physical gesture.<video_prompt[N]>Dynamic physical action (arrows releasing, army marching, sea churning, fire spreading), camera flyovers, sudden cinematic reveals.90–150 words, ONE continuous camera move, ONE clear subject action, stable ending frame.WORKFLOW PER EPISODESTEP 1: PREPARE INPUTSProvide:PlaintextType: A (Story) or B (Fact)
Title: [Optional]
Content: [Story source material or scriptural chapter]
STEP 2: RUN SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass)Outputs:Section 1: Scene breakdown with explicit Asset Type: IMAGE or Asset Type: VIDEO markers.Section 2: Timestamped narration.Section 2B: TTS-ready narration wrapped inside <script>...</script>.STEP 3: RUN PRODUCTION PROMPT (Mixed Asset Pass)Outputs:Section 3: Alternating visual blocks with sequential numbering:<image_prompt0> for 16:9 ThumbnailChronological tags matching the timeline (e.g., <video_prompt1>, <image_prompt2>, <video_prompt3>, <image_prompt4>)Section 4: Hindi text overlays.Section 5: Audience Reflection prompt.STEP 4: ASSEMBLEGenerate static images using <image_prompt[N]>.Generate video clips using <video_prompt[N]> (text-to-video or image-to-video using predecessor still).Synthesize narration from <script>.Assemble timeline in editor: hard cuts and subtle dissolves only.PART 2 — 🕉️ THE BIBLE (Static Reference)👥 CHARACTER BIBLE — NEVER CHANGE THESE DESCRIPTIONSRepeat full character descriptions verbatim in every visual prompt to guarantee consistency.🔵 RAMAAge: 25–30 years oldSkin: Deep blue-dark complexion ("shyama varna") — non-negotiable, never light or fairFace: Strong jaw, high forehead, calm and powerful eyes, slightly arched eyebrowsBody: Tall, broad shoulders, long arms reaching knees ("ajanubahu")Hair: Long black hair tied in an ascetic knot (jata) or warrior bunPalace attire: Yellow/gold silk dhoti, ornate crown (mukut), gold jewelry, bow SharangaForest/Exile attire: Ochre/saffron bark-cloth dhoti, matted hair, no crown, bow and quiverExpression: Dignified, compassionate, serene, divine majesty — never angry or anxious🌟 SITAAge: 20–25 years oldSkin: Golden-fair radiant complexion ("suvarna varna")Face: Large expressive eyes, gentle grace, oval face, long black hairPalace attire: Rich red and gold silk saree, elaborate traditional jewelryForest attire: Simple ochre or cream cotton saree, minimal wooden/seed jewelry, braided hairLanka captivity attire: Worn pale saree, unadorned, solemn dignity, sorrowful yet resilient eyesExpression: Graceful, resolute, devoted — never weak or helpless🏹 LAKSHMANAAge: 22–27 years oldSkin: Fair wheatish complexionFace: Sharp warrior features, intense alert eyes, strong jawBody: Highly athletic, muscular buildAttire: Similar to Rama's palette in green/ochre, carrying formidable longbow and quiverExpression: Fiercely vigilant, protective, intense loyalty🐒 HANUMANForm: Powerful Vanara warrior, golden-orange fur, upright muscular physique, tail arched gracefullyAttire: Simple sacred loincloth (kaupin), sacred thread (janeu), mace (gada)Expression: Deep devotional surrender, awe-inspiring strength, humble eyesScale: Explicitly specify normal human scale OR mountain-sized colossal form (vishwaroopa)👑 RAVANAAge: 40–50 years old appearance — imposing sovereignSkin: Dark bronze with fiery crimson undertoneFace: Ten heads (in wide establishing shots) OR dominant majestic central head (in close-ups)Attire: Black and blood-red royal silk, heavy gold armor, jeweled crowns, multiple armed weaponsExpression: Regal arrogance, unyielding pride, formidable authority — never cartoonish🗺️ LOCATION BIBLEAyodhya Palace: Treta Yuga Vedic stone architecture, colossal carved pillars, oil lamps, marigold drapes, sacred havan smoke, warm amber-gold light.Dandaka / Panchavati Forest: Dense primordial Indian jungle, towering sal/banyan trees, hanging roots, morning mist, sacred thatched ashram hut with a quiet dhuni fire.Chitrakuta: Peaceful sacred hills, clear streams, gentle deer, untouched natural serenity.Lanka: Imposing black stone and gold architecture atop jagged sea-cliffs, towering spires, dramatic stormy or twilight skies.Ashoka Vatika: Melancholic royal garden, weeping ashoka trees with scarlet blooms, oppressive luxury framing captivity.Kishkindha: Massive granite caves, carved mountain redoubts, waterfalls, primitive grandeur.Ram Setu / Ocean Shore: Craggy shoreline, endless churning ocean, massive floating sandstone boulders inscribed with holy names, vast Vanara host.⚠️ RELIGIOUS ACCURACY LAWRama must always have blue-dark skin.Treta Yuga setting only: absolute zero modern elements, modern clothing, or foreign architecture.Sacred Vedic attributes (tilak, janeu, agni, mudras) must be visually accurate.🖼️ UNIVERSAL NEGATIVE PROMPT (For All Image & Video Prompts)Plaintextcartoon, anime, 3d render, illustration, modern clothing, modern architecture, western facial features, plastic skin, wrong skin color for Rama (must be blue-dark, never fair), light-skinned Rama, disrespectful depiction, blurry, watermark, text in image, extra limbs, deformed hands, distorted anatomy, morphing faces, flickering, stuttering frames, camera jitter

### ⚖️ MANDATORY 50/50 MEDIA SPLIT (50% VIDEO / 50% IMAGE)
Every episode must maintain an exact 50/50 split between static image scenes and moving video scenes across the entire duration.
Follow an alternating rhythm throughout the timeline (Scene 1 MUST always be a video to hook the user):
- Odd scenes (Scene 1, Scene 3, Scene 5, ...): MOTION VIDEO CLIP (<video_prompt[N]>)
- Even scenes (Scene 2, Scene 4, Scene 6, ...): STATIC IMAGE (<image_prompt[N]>)
Ensure exactly 50% of the scenes are designated as image assets and 50% as video assets.

[ANCIENT DHARMA EDITORIAL RULES]
Apply these writing rules to Ancient Dharma episodes. For an explicitly unrelated topic, follow that topic's own tradition and audience instead of adding Hindu devotional language. These rules update the research, narration and closing instructions below; preserve every existing output section, extraction tag, asset number, media mode, character bible and narration-to-scene mapping. Perform the editorial work silently; do not add a new output section.

RESEARCH BEFORE COMMITTING TO A HOOK: Identify the actual source/version, what it supports, what belongs to a regional retelling, and what is interpretation. Establish one central dilemma, the strongest supported detail, the decisive choice and the real outcome. Treat any preselected retention hook as provisional: revise its wording and promise when the research does not support it. Never invent dialogue, motives, quotations, miracles as scientific proof, or scriptural attribution to make a hook work. Keep source notes in the existing production notes, with a brief natural attribution in speech where necessary.

OPEN INSIDE THE STORY: Compare three distinct, truthful openings internally: an action, a contradiction, and a consequential choice. Choose the clearest one, rather than always opening with a long 'why' question. Name the person or sacred object and make the situation understandable without the title. Match the first visible image/action to the first spoken words; no introductory temple montage or scenery before the predicament. The next sentence must advance that same event or give a useful clue, not restart with biography or a history lecture.

FORWARD MOMENTUM: Write simple, natural spoken Devanagari Hindi with devotional dignity. Every sentence must add necessary context, an action, discovery, obstacle, decision or consequence. Connect beats through cause and effect. Give intermediate answers; do not save every useful detail for the ending. Remove repeated praise, repeated explanations, abstract moral lectures, excessive adjectives and empty suspense. Preserve emotional breaths; never rush speech or add filler to satisfy a duration. Build emotion from supported events, not invented private thoughts.

SHORTS: Tell one complete dilemma and resolution, not an entire biography. Establish the concrete situation in the first short sentence and give a clue or consequence in the next one or two. Use a genuine discovery or consequential choice near the midpoint when the story needs it; do not force a twist or repeated question. Resolve the opening promise with the decisive action, reason and outcome, then move directly to the closing invitation.

ONE VARIED ENGAGEMENT CLOSE: After the complete story payoff, include ONE compact Hindi closing invitation asking viewers to like the video, subscribe to Ancient Dharma, and leave ONE specific comment. Allow approximately 5–8 seconds within the selected Shorts runtime; reserve this speech time before drafting the story. Do not try to squeeze all three requests into a three-second blessing. Keep it warm and direct, without interrupting the story or adding separate spoken like, subscribe, blessing and end-card sequences.

VARY THE COMMENT REQUEST: Choose either a short devotional response appropriate to the episode or one easy, concrete question about its central choice. Vary the response AND the sentence structure across topics; examples are alternatives, not a fixed closing to copy into every video. Ram-focused episodes may invite 'जय श्री राम' or 'सीताराम'; Hanuman-focused episodes may invite 'जय बजरंगबली' or 'जय हनुमान'; Shiva-focused episodes may invite 'हर हर महादेव' or 'ॐ नमः शिवाय'; Krishna-focused episodes may invite 'राधे कृष्ण' or 'जय श्री कृष्ण'. Never force a Ram greeting into an unrelated tradition. For a dilemma, ask a brief question such as 'भरत के किस निर्णय ने आपको सबसे अधिक छुआ?' instead of a generic 'आपकी क्या राय है?'. Invite one response, not a list of questions.

Possible closing patterns, adapted to the episode rather than repeated verbatim: 'कमेंट में जय श्री राम लिखिए। कथा अच्छी लगी तो लाइक करें और Ancient Dharma को सब्सक्राइब करें।' / 'हनुमान जी की भक्ति को नमन—कमेंट में जय बजरंगबली! ऐसी कथाओं के लिए लाइक करें और चैनल सब्सक्राइब करें।' / 'भरत के किस निर्णय ने आपका मन छुआ? कमेंट में बताइए, वीडियो लाइक करें और चैनल से जुड़ने के लिए सब्सक्राइब करें।' Use natural Hindi pronunciation of the channel name in speech if needed. Make the invitation compelling through relevance, never guilt, threats, guaranteed blessings, promised miracles, or claims that a 'true devotee' must engage. Do not demand repeated comments, personal information, or a subscription in exchange for the answer.

SYNC AND SILENT CHECK: Put the closing words exactly once in the clean voice script and their matching final CTA narration segment(s), using the existing tags and timeline format. Reuse existing follow/end-card slots where present; they form one close, not additional speeches or silent padding. Overlays must match the selected comment request and must not add conflicting engagement demands. Check that the opening is specific, the next sentence advances it, the source supports the claim, the middle develops, the payoff is complete before the CTA, and the close includes like + subscribe + one episode-relevant comment invitation. Do not output these checks or predict retention scores.
[/ANCIENT DHARMA EDITORIAL RULES]

PART 3 — 🕉️ SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass — Run FIRST)Take raw content and output a locked Hindi script. Define asset types for every single beat.Script Architecture Rules:Hook Rule: The first 3–6 spoken words must begin a concrete, source-supported action, dilemma or contrast with immediate emotional stakes. Complete a clear opening thought within the first 1–3 seconds; name the relevant person or sacred object instead of a vague "this" or "he". Let the unanswered question arise from why the action matters, not from hiding who is involved. No channel greetings, series titles, background lecture or invented sacred dialogue. Keep the central question clear while giving an early concrete answer, clue or consequence in the next one or two sentences. Every following sentence must change what the viewer knows, what the protagonist can do, or what the choice will cost. Connect beats through cause and effect; cut repeated setup, biography before the predicament, redundant adjectives and generic suspense. Aim for a meaningful development about every 5–8 seconds where the story supports it, inside the existing scene structure; this is a writing guide, not a cut, scene-count or speech-speed requirement. Use short, natural spoken sentences, clear subjects and concrete verbs. Never hide basic context just to manufacture curiosity. Silently compare three different opening lines and use the clearest, most specific one that the story actually pays off; output only the chosen line in the existing format. Read the opening without the title: the viewer must understand the situation and have a specific reason to hear the next sentence. Remove any line that adds neither necessary context nor a new development. These are editorial choices, not guaranteed audience metrics.Midpoint Re-Hook: At 50–60% mark, use a concise source-supported discovery, decision or consequence that changes the meaning of an earlier detail or raises the cost of the next action. Follow the 5–8 word turn with its concrete explanation; do not merely announce that a twist is coming. Preserve devotional dignity and source fidelity. A smaller resolved question should lead naturally into the remaining central question.Language: Simple, poignant, spoken Devanagari Hindi with temple-katha resonance.Ending: Complete the story and its promised payoff first. Then give ONE varied Hindi closing invitation to like, subscribe and leave one episode-relevant comment, following the editorial rules above. Reserve approximately 5–8 seconds within the selected runtime. Use the existing follow/end-card slots as one close; no separate repeated blessing, recap or extra engagement requests. Finish the story on its concrete consequence before the invitation.

# Production Research Dossier: Abhimanyu & The Chakravyuha

**Topic:** Abhimanyu and the Chakravyuha: The 16-Year-Old Warrior Who Shook the Kaurava Army  
**Target Video Duration:** ~90 Seconds  
**Format / Platform:** YouTube Shorts / Vertical Video (9:16)  
**Narration & Dialogue Language:** Pure Spoken Devanagari Hindi (Natural, dramatic, dignified)  
**Primary Source:** *Vyasa Mahabharata* (Drona Parva – Abhimanyu-vadha Parva)  

---

## 1. Verified Facts, Background & Key Data

### Core Historical & Epic Context
* **The Setting:** Day 13 of the 18-day Kurukshetra War. 
* **The Strategic Trap:** To capture King Yudhishthira alive and end the war, Dronacharya (Kaurava Commander-in-Chief) designed the **Chakravyuha** (or *Padmavyuha*)—a multi-tiered, constantly rotating lotus/wheel battle formation.
* **The Diversion:** Drona arranged for the Samshaptakas to draw Arjuna and Lord Krishna away to the far southern side of the battlefield, as Arjuna was the primary warrior who knew how to breach and exit the formation.
* **Abhimanyu’s Secret Knowledge:** 16-year-old Abhimanyu (son of Arjuna and Subhadra, Krishna’s nephew) had absorbed the secret technique of entering/breaching the outer rings of the Chakravyuha while still in his mother’s womb when Arjuna described it to Subhadra. However, Subhadra fell asleep before Arjuna could explain the exit strategy; thus, Abhimanyu knew only how to pierce the entrance, not how to come out.
* **The Pandava Plan & Jayadratha’s Blockade:** Abhimanyu agreed to pierce the formation on the condition that Yudhishthira, Bhima, Satyaki, and the Pandava army would follow right behind him. However, Jayadratha (King of Sindhu), empowered by Shiva's boon, single-handedly held off all the Pandava elders at the gate, trapping 16-year-old Abhimanyu inside alone.
* **The Seven Maharathis & The Adharmic Assault:** Trapped inside, Abhimanyu decimated thousands of Kaurava soldiers and defeated elite warriors including Drona, Karna, Duryodhana, Kripacharya, Ashwatthama, Shalya, and Kritavarma, even slaying Duryodhana's son Lakshmana. Realizing he could not be defeated in fair single combat (*Dharma-yuddha*), six to seven Maharathis broke all codes of war simultaneously:
  1. Karna, on Drona's instruction, severed Abhimanyu’s bow from behind.
  2. His charioteer and horses were killed.
  3. His chariot was smashed and his armor/shield broken.
* **The Iconic Last Stand:** Weaponless and grounded, Abhimanyu hoisted a giant wooden chariot wheel like a Sudarshana Chakra, fighting off heavily armed Maharathis until he was struck from behind with a mace by Duhshasana’s son.
* **Cosmic Identity:** In the *Adi Parva*, Abhimanyu is revealed as the earthly incarnation of **Varchas**, son of the Moon God (Soma). Soma agreed to let his son take birth on Earth for only 16 years to destroy the Kaurava forces before returning.

---

## 2. Chronological Story Arc & Scene Beats (~90s)

> **Zero Narrator Mandate:** There is NO narrator ([सूत्रधार]). All context, drama, action, and resolution must be delivered through direct, conversational character dialogue ([द्रोणाचार्य], [अभिमन्यु], [दुर्योधन], [कर्ण]).

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                           DRAMATIC TIMELINE                             │
│                                                                         │
│  [00:00 - 00:18] Scene 1: The Entrance Confrontation (Drona vs Abhimanyu)│
│  [00:18 - 00:38] Scene 2: Piercing the Outer Rings (Duryodhana's Panic) │
│  [00:38 - 00:60] Scene 3: The Adharmic Trap Inside (Karna & Drona)      │
│  [00:60 - 00:78] Scene 4: The Chariot Wheel Last Stand                  │
│  [00:78 - 00:90] Scene 5: Immortal Sacrifice & Final CTA               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Beat 1: The Gate Confrontation (00:00 – 00:18)
* **Visual:** Close-up of Guru Dronacharya in ornate gilded armor at the mouth of the massive, rotating, wheel-like Chakravyuha formation. Beside him, 16-year-old Abhimanyu stands on his chariot with a golden bow.
* **Spoken Dialogue:**
  * **[द्रोणाचार्य]:** "अभिमन्यु, इस चक्रव्यूह का भेद केवल तुम्हारे पिता अर्जुन जानते हैं, तुम पीछे हट जाओ!"
  * **[अभिमन्यु]:** "गुरुदेव! पांडव वीर धर्म के युद्ध में पीछे नहीं हटते। आज १६ वर्ष का यह बालक आपके चक्रव्यूह के दांत तोड़ेगा!"

### Beat 2: Breaching the Formation & Kaurava Panic (00:18 – 00:38)
* **Visual:** Abhimanyu’s chariot breaches the outer ring. Arrows fly rapidly, shattering Kaurava defenses. Duryodhana watches in horror as his son Lakshmana falls.
* **Spoken Dialogue:**
  * **[दुर्योधन]:** "आचार्य! यह बालक नहीं, साक्षात काल है! इसने हमारे व्यूह को चीर दिया और मेरे पुत्र का वध कर दिया!"
  * **[अभिमन्यु]:** "दुर्योधन! अधर्म की नींव पर खड़ी सेना अर्जुन के पुत्र को चक्रव्यूह में बंदी नहीं बना सकती!"

### Beat 3: The Unlawful Trap & Broken Bow (00:38 – 00:60)
* **Visual:** Jayadratha seals the entrance behind Abhimanyu. Seven Maharathis (Drona, Karna, Duryodhana, etc.) encircle the isolated youth. Karna hesitates, bow drawn.
* **Spoken Dialogue:**
  * **[कर्ण]:** "आचार्य, जब तक इसके हाथ में धनुष है, इस वीर को सम्मुख युद्ध में हराना असंभव है!"
  * **[द्रोणाचार्य]:** "तो पीछे से प्रहार करो कर्ण! इसका धनुष काट दो, यही इसे रोकने का एकमात्र मार्ग है!"
  * **[अभिमन्यु]:** "सामने से प्रहार करने का साहस खो चुके हो? धनुष टूटेगा, फिर भी मेरा क्षत्रिय धर्म नहीं टूटेगा!"

### Beat 4: The Chariot Wheel Last Stand (00:60 – 00:78)
* **Visual:** His bow cut, chariot destroyed, and horses slain, Abhimanyu leaps to the ground, hoists a giant wooden chariot wheel above his head like a divine chakra, and charges the armed Maharathis.
* **Spoken Dialogue:**
  * **[अभिमन्यु]:** "सात-सात महारथी मिलकर एक निहत्थे बालक पर छल करते हैं? देखो, बिना धनुष के भी पांडव का रक्त कैसे लड़ता है!"
  * **[दुर्योधन]:** "आक्रमण करो! इस रथ के पहिए को भी तोड़ दो, वरना यह अकेला हमारी पूरी सेना को नष्ट कर देगा!"

### Beat 5: Immortal Legacy & Natural CTA Close (00:78 – 00:90)
* **Visual:** Golden twilight over Kurukshetra. Abhimanyu stands heroically amidst fallen weapons before his eternal sacrifice.
* **Spoken Dialogue:**
  * **[द्रोणाचार्य]:** "इतिहास तुम्हें कभी नहीं भूलेगा, वीर अभिमन्यु! तुम्हारा त्याग युगों-युगों तक अमर रहेगा।"
  * **[अभिमन्यु]:** "धर्म के लिए दिया गया बलिदान कभी व्यर्थ नहीं जाता! अभिमन्यु के इस अदम्य साहस को नमन करें—कमेंट में 'जय श्री कृष्ण' लिखिए! यह गाथा अच्छी लगी हो तो वीडियो को लाइक करें और Ancient Dharma को सब्सक्राइब करें!"

### Setting & Environment

[अभिमन्यु]: गुरुदेव! पांडव वीर धर्म युद्ध में कभी पीछे नहीं हटते! आज यह १६ वर्ष का बालक आपके चक्रव्यूह के दांत तोड़ेगा!

[द्रोणाचार्य]: यह बालक आंधी की तरह व्यूह की पंक्तियों को रोंदता हुआ भीतर घुस आया है!

[दुर्योधन]: आचार्य! यह १६ साल का बालक नहीं, साक्षात काल है! इसने हमारे व्यूह को चीर दिया और मेरे पुत्र का वध कर दिया!

[अभिमन्यु]: दुर्योधन! अधर्म की नींव पर खड़ी कौरव सेना, अर्जुन के पुत्र को चक्रव्यूह में बंदी नहीं बना सकती!

[द्रोणाचार्य]: जयद्रथ ने बाहर पांडवों का मार्ग रोक लिया है... अभिमन्यु अब व्यूह के भीतर अकेला घिर चुका है!

[दुर्योधन]: सातों महारथी एक साथ इसे घेर लो! इसे जीवित बाहर नहीं निकलने देना है!

[कर्ण]: आचार्य, जब तक इसके हाथ में यह दिव्यास्त्र धनुष है, इस वीर को सम्मुख युद्ध में परास्त करना असंभव है!

[द्रोणाचार्य]: तो पीछे से प्रहार करो कर्ण! इसका धनुष काट दो, यही इसे रोकने का एकमात्र मार्ग है!

[अभिमन्यु]: सामने से लड़ने का साहस खो चुके हो? धनुष टूटेगा, फिर भी मेरा क्षत्रिय धर्म नहीं टूटेगा!

[दुर्योधन]: इसके रथ के घोड़ों को मार दो! इसका रथ छिन्न-भिन्न कर दो!

[अभिमन्यु]: निहत्था करके भी पांडव के रक्त को पराजित नहीं कर पाओगे!

[अभिमन्यु]: सात-सात महारथी मिलकर एक निहत्थे बालक पर छल करते हैं? देखो, बिना धनुष के भी पांडव का तेज कैसे चमकता है!

[दुर्योधन]: आक्रमण करो! इस रथ के पहिए को भी तोड़ दो, वरना यह अकेला हमारी सेना का संहार कर देगा!

[द्रोणाचार्य]: इतिहास तुम्हें कभी नहीं भूलेगा, वीर अभिमन्यु! तुम्हारा यह अदम्य त्याग युगों-युगों तक अमर रहेगा!

[अभिमन्यु]: धर्म के लिए दिया गया बलिदान कभी व्यर्थ नहीं जाता! वीर अभिमन्यु के इस अदम्य साहस को नमन करें—कमेंट में 'जय श्री कृष्ण' लिखिए! कथा अच्छी लगी हो तो वीडियो को लाइक करें और Ancient Dharma को सब्सक्राइब करें!

STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)Before writing a single word of narration or any image/video prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic and Source Material. Do not skip this. A shallow script produces a failed video.Research silently and establish:Verified core facts — what actually happened, who was involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, and popular myth.The single strongest HOOK ANGLE — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for.The core EMOTION of this episode (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.Visual opportunities — which moments require static, frozen emotional weight and which demand continuous, cinematic motion (era, location, costume, light, scale, kinetic action).Uncertainties — anything sources disagree on or you cannot verify. NEVER invent quotations, Sanskrit verses, dates, statistics, dialogue from scripture, or miracles presented as scientific proof. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly.Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation.🕉️ RAMAYANA — ADI KAVYAMASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 8.0 HYBRID MIXED MEDIABible + Script Prompt + Mixed Production Prompt (Images & Videos) + Workflow GuideThis document establishes the HYBRID MIXED-SCRIPT PIPELINE. It combines static visual stills and cinematic generative AI video clips into a single chronological timeline.🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOLThe pipeline uses three and only three functional tag families:Narration Tag: <script>...</script> — Houses the complete, raw, TTS-ready Devanagari Hindi audio narration in Section 2B.Auto-Incrementing Visual Tags: Sequential visual prompts matching the exact timeline order across both static and moving formats:<image_prompt[N]>...</image_prompt[N]> for static frames (Midjourney, Flux, Leonardo.AI).<video_prompt[N]>...</video_prompt[N]> for motion shots (Runway Gen-3, Luma Dream Machine, Sora, Kling).Crucial Rule: The first scene (Scene 1) MUST ALWAYS be a video (<video_prompt1>) to hook the user immediately. The index counter [N] increments chronologically across the entire video regardless of asset type: e.g., <video_prompt1>, <image_prompt2>, <video_prompt3>, <image_prompt4>.Thumbnail Tag: Always locked to <image_prompt0>...</image_prompt0>.📑 TABLE OF CONTENTSWORKFLOW GUIDE — Mixed script rules and asset selectionTHE BIBLE — Static reference (Character Bible, Location Bible, Visual Style, Religious Accuracy Law, Negative Prompts)SCRIPT PROMPT — Creative pass (run first)PRODUCTION PROMPT — Mixed asset generation pass (run second)PART 1 — 🕉️ WORKFLOW GUIDEHow to Manage the Mixed Media PipelineDECISION MATRIX: IMAGE VS. VIDEONot every scene should be video. Overusing video creates visual fatigue, morphing artifacts, and pacing breaks. Distribute assets deliberately:Asset TypeBest Used ForProduction Standard<image_prompt[N]>Emotional portraits, theological/sacred moments, heavy-detail environments, dialogue pauses, moments requiring zero anatomical distortion.70–140 words, hyper-detailed composition, frozen physical gesture.<video_prompt[N]>Dynamic physical action (arrows releasing, army marching, sea churning, fire spreading), camera flyovers, sudden cinematic reveals.90–150 words, ONE continuous camera move, ONE clear subject action, stable ending frame.WORKFLOW PER EPISODESTEP 1: PREPARE INPUTSProvide:PlaintextType: A (Story) or B (Fact)
Title: [Optional]
Content: [Story source material or scriptural chapter]
STEP 2: RUN SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass)Outputs:Section 1: Scene breakdown with explicit Asset Type: IMAGE or Asset Type: VIDEO markers.Section 2: Timestamped narration.Section 2B: TTS-ready narration wrapped inside <script>...</script>.STEP 3: RUN PRODUCTION PROMPT (Mixed Asset Pass)Outputs:Section 3: Alternating visual blocks with sequential numbering:<image_prompt0> for 16:9 ThumbnailChronological tags matching the timeline (e.g., <video_prompt1>, <image_prompt2>, <video_prompt3>, <image_prompt4>)Section 4: Hindi text overlays.Section 5: Audience Reflection prompt.STEP 4: ### ⚖️ MANDATORY 50/50 MEDIA SPLIT (50% VIDEO / 50% IMAGE)
Every episode must maintain an exact 50/50 split between static image scenes and moving video scenes across the entire duration.
Follow an alternating rhythm throughout the timeline (Scene 1 MUST always be a video to hook the user):
- Odd scenes (Scene 1, Scene 3, Scene 5, ...): MOTION VIDEO CLIP (<video_prompt[N]>)
- Even scenes (Scene 2, Scene 4, Scene 6, ...): STATIC IMAGE (<image_prompt[N]>)
Ensure exactly 50% of the scenes are designated as image assets and 50% as video assets.

[ANCIENT DHARMA EDITORIAL RULES]
Apply these writing rules to Ancient Dharma episodes. For an explicitly unrelated topic, follow that topic's own tradition and audience instead of adding Hindu devotional language. These rules update the research, narration and closing instructions below; preserve every existing output section, extraction tag, asset number, media mode, character bible and narration-to-scene mapping. Perform the editorial work silently; do not add a new output section.

RESEARCH BEFORE COMMITTING TO A HOOK: Identify the actual source/version, what it supports, what belongs to a regional retelling, and what is interpretation. Establish one central dilemma, the strongest supported detail, the decisive choice and the real outcome. Treat any preselected retention hook as provisional: revise its wording and promise when the research does not support it. Never invent dialogue, motives, quotations, miracles as scientific proof, or scriptural attribution to make a hook work. Keep source notes in the existing production notes, with a brief natural attribution in speech where necessary.

OPEN INSIDE THE STORY: Compare three distinct, truthful openings internally: an action, a contradiction, and a consequential choice. Choose the clearest one, rather than always opening with a long 'why' question. Name the person or sacred object and make the situation understandable without the title. Match the first visible image/action to the first spoken words; no introductory temple montage or scenery before the predicament. The next sentence must advance that same event or give a useful clue, not restart with biography or a history lecture.

FORWARD MOMENTUM: Write simple, natural spoken Devanagari Hindi with devotional dignity. Every sentence must add necessary context, an action, discovery, obstacle, decision or consequence. Connect beats through cause and effect. Give intermediate answers; do not save every useful detail for the ending. Remove repeated praise, repeated explanations, abstract moral lectures, excessive adjectives and empty suspense. Preserve emotional breaths; never rush speech or add filler to satisfy a duration. Build emotion from supported events, not invented private thoughts.

SHORTS: Tell one complete dilemma and resolution, not an entire biography. Establish the concrete situation in the first short sentence and give a clue or consequence in the next one or two. Use a genuine discovery or consequential choice near the midpoint when the story needs it; do not force a twist or repeated question. Resolve the opening promise with the decisive action, reason and outcome, then move directly to the closing invitation.

ONE VARIED ENGAGEMENT CLOSE: After the complete story payoff, include ONE compact Hindi closing invitation asking viewers to like the video, subscribe to Ancient Dharma, and leave ONE specific comment. Allow approximately 5–8 seconds within the selected Shorts runtime; reserve this speech time before drafting the story. Do not try to squeeze all three requests into a three-second blessing. Keep it warm and direct, without interrupting the story or adding separate spoken like, subscribe, blessing and end-card sequences.

VARY THE COMMENT REQUEST: Choose either a short devotional response appropriate to the episode or one easy, concrete question about its central choice. Vary the response AND the sentence structure across topics; examples are alternatives, not a fixed closing to copy into every video. Ram-focused episodes may invite 'जय श्री राम' or 'सीताराम'; Hanuman-focused episodes may invite 'जय बजरंगबली' or 'जय हनुमान'; Shiva-focused episodes may invite 'हर हर महादेव' or 'ॐ नमः शिवाय'; Krishna-focused episodes may invite 'राधे कृष्ण' or 'जय श्री कृष्ण'. Never force a Ram greeting into an unrelated tradition. For a dilemma, ask a brief question such as 'भरत के किस निर्णय ने आपको सबसे अधिक छुआ?' instead of a generic 'आपकी क्या राय है?'. Invite one response, not a list of questions.

Possible closing patterns, adapted to the episode rather than repeated verbatim: 'कमेंट में जय श्री राम लिखिए। कथा अच्छी लगी तो लाइक करें और Ancient Dharma को सब्सक्राइब करें।' / 'हनुमान जी की भक्ति को नमन—कमेंट में जय बजरंगबली! ऐसी कथाओं के लिए लाइक करें और चैनल सब्सक्राइब करें।' / 'भरत के किस निर्णय ने आपका मन छुआ? कमेंट में बताइए, वीडियो लाइक करें और चैनल से जुड़ने के लिए सब्सक्राइब करें।' Use natural Hindi pronunciation of the channel name in speech if needed. Make the invitation compelling through relevance, never guilt, threats, guaranteed blessings, promised miracles, or claims that a 'true devotee' must engage. Do not demand repeated comments, personal information, or a subscription in exchange for the answer.

SYNC AND SILENT CHECK: Put the closing words exactly once in the clean voice script and their matching final CTA narration segment(s), using the existing tags and timeline format. Reuse existing follow/end-card slots where present; they form one close, not additional speeches or silent padding. Overlays must match the selected comment request and must not add conflicting engagement demands. Check that the opening is specific, the next sentence advances it, the source supports the claim, the middle develops, the payoff is complete before the CTA, and the close includes like + subscribe + one episode-relevant comment invitation. Do not output these checks or predict retention scores.
[/ANCIENT DHARMA EDITORIAL RULES]

PART 3 — 🕉️ SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass — Run FIRST)Take raw content and output a locked Hindi script. Define asset types for every single beat.Script Architecture Rules:Hook Rule: The first 3–6 spoken words must begin a concrete, source-supported action, dilemma or contrast with immediate emotional stakes. Complete a clear opening thought within the first 1–3 seconds; name the relevant person or sacred object instead of a vague "this" or "he". Let the unanswered question arise from why the action matters, not from hiding who is involved. No channel greetings, series titles, background lecture or invented sacred dialogue. Keep the central question clear while giving an early concrete answer, clue or consequence in the next one or two sentences. Every following sentence must change what the viewer knows, what the protagonist can do, or what the choice will cost. Connect beats through cause and effect; cut repeated setup, biography before the predicament, redundant adjectives and generic suspense. Aim for a meaningful development about every 5–8 seconds where the story supports it, inside the existing scene structure; this is a writing guide, not a cut, scene-count or speech-speed requirement. Use short, natural spoken sentences, clear subjects and concrete verbs. Never hide basic context just to manufacture curiosity. Silently compare three different opening lines and use the clearest, most specific one that the story actually pays off; output only the chosen line in the existing format. Read the opening without the title: the viewer must understand the situation and have a specific reason to hear the next sentence. Remove any line that adds neither necessary context nor a new development. These are editorial choices, not guaranteed audience metrics.Midpoint Re-Hook: At 50–60% mark, use a concise source-supported discovery, decision or consequence that changes the meaning of an earlier detail or raises the cost of the next action. Follow the 5–8 word turn with its concrete explanation; do not merely announce that a twist is coming. Preserve devotional dignity and source fidelity. A smaller resolved question should lead naturally into the remaining central question.Language: Simple, poignant, spoken Devanagari Hindi with temple-katha resonance.Ending: Complete the story and its promised payoff first. Then give ONE varied Hindi closing invitation to like, subscribe and leave one episode-relevant comment, following the editorial rules above. Reserve approximately 5–8 seconds within the selected runtime. Use the existing follow/end-card slots as one close; no separate repeated blessing, recap or extra engagement requests. Finish the story on its concrete consequence before the invitation.

PART 4 — 🕉️ PRODUCTION PROMPT (Mixed Media Asset Pass — Run SECOND)Your job is to translate the locked script into self-contained generation prompts using the dynamic incrementing tag system.Mixed Media Asset Standards:1. howItWorks: Research runs first, then the script extracts assets. Generate or import images, import videos, then generate narration and render a portrait Short. Every image prompt is 70-120 words and every video prompt 90-150 words with a scroll-stopping hook. Turn off Use video imports in Generation for images only.

graphics.style: Let AI choose only moments where a graphic materially explains the narration. Metadata is a suggestion, never a command to decorate every scene. Leave ordinary footage clean, keep breathing room between beats, and allow zero graphics. No cards, panels, boxed labels, enclosing frames, blur backings or photo badges. Use free-floating type, fine lines and purposeful diagrams in open space around subjects. Never invent facts, coordinates, source labels or telemetry. Preview the actual result before export.

retentionPlan.structure: Source-supported action, contradiction or consequential choice → authentic traditional story with connected discoveries and intermediate answers → decisive reason and outcome → one brief, varied Hindi invitation to like, subscribe and leave an episode-relevant comment.
retentionPlan.viewerPromise: Discover the profound final spiritual lesson and kingly duties (Rajadharma) imparted by Bhishma to Yudhishthira from his bed of arrows, revealing why the grand patriarch had to wait for Utterayana to pass away.

hooks.openingLine: युधिष्ठिर, सरशैया पर लेटे पितामह भीष्म के पास क्षमा मांगने नहीं, बल्कि धर्म का अंतिम सत्य सीखने आए थे।
hooks.openingVisual: Dramatic close-up of young King Yudhishthira kneeling with folded hands beside Grandsire Bhishma, who lies severely wounded on a bed of arrows on the battlefield of Kurukshetra at sunset.
hooks.curiosity: Why would a newly crowned king seek political and spiritual guidance from a dying patriarch lying on a bed of painful arrows?
hooks.payoff: The realization that Bhishma held back his death through Iccha Mrityu to deliver the essential duties of kingship (Rajadharma) and Moksha Dharma to preserve the future of Bharat.
hooks.reason: Directly identifies the central characters and their high-stakes setting while reframing Yudhishthira's visit from grief to a vital search for divine knowledge.

hooks.openingLine: तीरों की शैया पर तड़पते हुए भी पितामह भीष्म ने अपने प्राण क्यों रोके रखे थे?
hooks.openingVisual: Wide cinematic shot of Bhishma lying on sharp arrows, surrounded by the Pandavas and Bhagavan Krishna, as golden light radiates around his head.
hooks.curiosity: What secret purpose kept Bhishma alive despite sustaining mortal arrow wounds throughout his entire body?
hooks.payoff: Bhishma was waiting for the auspicious Uttarayana while transmitting the sacred Vishnu Sahasranama and Rajadharma to Yudhishthira.
hooks.reason: Emphasizes the striking visual anomaly of Bhishma's physical suffering contrasted with his absolute spiritual control over his life force.

hooks.openingLine: महाभारत युद्ध के बाद जब सम्राट युधिष्ठिर का मन ग्लानि से भर गया, तब श्री कृष्ण उन्हें कहां ले गए?
hooks.openingVisual: Lord Krishna guiding a sorrowful Yudhishthira through the quiet, misty remains of Kurukshetra towards the reclining figure of Bhishma.
hooks.curiosity: How did Krishna resolve Yudhishthira's intense guilt over the destruction caused by the war?
hooks.payoff: Krishna directed Yudhishthira to Bhishma, the ultimate authority on Dharma, whose dying words restored Yudhishthira's resolve to rule with righteousness.
hooks.reason: Establishes the emotional dilemma of Yudhishthira's remorse immediately following the Great War and points directly to the source of his healing.

**On-Screen Text:** सभा का मौन क्यों?

**Text:** [भीष्म]: "पुत्र! उस समय मैं अधर्म का अन्न खा रहा था, जिससे मेरी बुद्धि मलिन थी! अर्जुन के बाणों ने वह दुष्ट रक्त बहाकर मुझे पवित्र कर दिया!"

**On-Screen Text:** विष्णु सहस्रनाम का जन्म

**Text:** [श्री कृष्ण]: "पितामह का यह अमर ज्ञान संपूर्ण भारतवर्ष के धर्म की नींव बनेगा, युधिष्ठिर।"

**On-Screen Text:** धर्म की अमर नींव

**On-Screen Text:** संशय का अंत

**Duration:** 01:18–01:24 (6s)  
**Asset Type:** VIDEO

**On-Screen Text:** धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः

**Asset Type:** VIDEO
